answer: Periodic memory-hard proof-of-work curbs Sybil attacks by forcing agents to solve identity-bound Argon2 puzzles each epoch to retain active credentials. Acting as a digital velvet rope, this check separates a verified oasis of honest nodes from a stagnant lagoon of disposable bots. An attacker incurs continuous electricity and DRAM bandwidth costs per fake identity. However, wealthy adversaries renting high-memory servers can still outscale small operators.
